Introduction and meaning
Voyeurism. BNS restatement of IPC 354C. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 354C. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 77 is the rule on “Voyeurism”. The section provides that whoever watches, or captures the image of a woman engaging in a private act in circumstances where she would usually have the expectation of not being observed either by the perpetrator or by any other person at the behest of the perpetrator or disseminates such image shall be punished on first conviction with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than one year, but which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine, and be punished on a second or subsequent conviction, with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than three years, but which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 77 exists so that “Voyeurism” has a closed legal test in Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Sexual offences, assault, marriage, miscarriage, and offences against the child — placed first among the offence chapters.

The provision in detail
77. Whoever watches, or captures the image of a woman engaging in a private act in circumstances where she would usually have the expectation of not being observed either by the perpetrator or by any other person at the behest of the perpetrator or disseminates such image shall be punished on first conviction with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than one year, but which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine, and be punished on a second or subsequent conviction, with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than three years, but which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine

Definitions and key terms
“private act” — an act of watching carried out in a place which, in the circumstances, would reasonably be expected to provide privacy and where the victim’s genitals, posterior or breasts are exposed or covered only in underwear.

Essential ingredients
1. Whoever watches, or captures the image of a woman engaging in a private act in circumstances where she would usually have the expectation of not being observed either by the perpetrator or by any other person at the behest of the perpetrator or disseminates such image shall be punished on first conviction with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than one year, but which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine, and be punished on a second or subsequent conviction, with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than three years, but which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine

Explanations
Explanation 1.—For the purposes of this section, “private act” includes an act of watching carried out in a place which, in the circumstances, would reasonably be expected to provide privacy and where the victim’s genitals, posterior or breasts are exposed or covered only in underwear; or the victim is using a lavatory; or the victim is doing a sexual act that is not of a kind ordinarily done in public

Explanation 2.—Where the victim consents to the capture of the images or any act, but not to their dissemination to third persons and where such image or act is disseminated, such dissemination shall be considered an offence under this section

hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 77 (Voyeurism) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.
hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 77 (Voyeurism), Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) Whoever watches, or captures the image of a woman engaging in a private act in circumstances where she would usually have the expectation of not being observed either by the perpetrator or by any other person at the behest of the perpetrator or disseminates such image shall be punished on first conviction with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than one year, but which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine, and be punished on a second or subsequent conviction, with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than three years, but which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine
Step 3 — Read every Explanation. An explanation is part of the section. Omitting it leaves the analysis incomplete and vulnerable to rebuttal.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 77 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

learningObjectives: Understand the cyber and physical privacy offence of voyeurism under BNS s. 77.
Analyze the core concepts: 'private act' and 'reasonable expectation of privacy'.
Examine capturing, watching, and dissemination as distinct modes of violation.
Master the two-tier sentencing: 1 to 3 years for first conviction; 3 to 7 years for subsequent.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 77 provides that any man who watches, or captures the image of a woman engaging in a private act in circumstances where she would usually have the expectation of not being observed either by the perpetrator or by any other person at the behest of the perpetrator, or disseminates such image, shall be punished: (a) on first conviction with imprisonment of either description for a term not less than one year but which may extend to three years, and fine; and (b) on second or subsequent conviction with imprisonment not less than three years but which may extend to seven years, and fine. Explanations define 'private act' and consensual capture followed by non-consensual dissemination.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: A woman's right to privacy in her personal and intimate bodily sphere is an absolute right. Secretly watching, recording, or disseminating images of private acts violates constitutional dignity and is penalized as voyeurism.
statutoryFramework: Chapter V — Of Offences against Women and Children, BNS s. 77 (corresponding to IPC s. 354C).
Conduct: Watches, captures image, OR disseminates image.
Context: Woman engaging in a 'private act' with expectation of privacy.
Explanation 1: 'Private act' includes an act of watching/capture in a place which reasonably yields privacy (using lavatory, undressing, sexual act).
Explanation 2: If the woman consented to capture but DID NOT consent to dissemination, the dissemination constitutes voyeurism.
First conviction: 1 to 3 years imprisonment and fine.
Subsequent conviction: 3 to 7 years imprisonment and fine.
essentialIngredients: The woman was engaging in a private act in circumstances where she had a reasonable expectation of privacy.
The accused watched her, captured her image, or disseminated the image.
Or under Explanation 2, the accused disseminated images captured with consent without authorization.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 77 addresses modern optical and digital surveillance abuses (hidden cameras in hotel rooms, fitting rooms, public restrooms, and unauthorized video sharing). A 'private act' encompasses showering, undressing, using the toilet, or engaging in intimate sexual activity in a secluded space. Crucially, Explanation 2 addresses 'revenge porn' and intimate betrayal: even if a woman voluntarily shared an intimate photograph with her partner in private, the partner has NO right to forward or upload that image to third parties or online platforms; doing so constitutes voyeurism.
examples: Teaching example (Hidden camera in trial room): A clothing store manager installs a hidden spy-camera in the female changing room and records customers undressing. Section 77 directly applies; he faces up to 3 years imprisonment on first conviction.

Teaching example (Non-consensual dissemination / Revenge porn): A woman shares an intimate video with her boyfriend in confidence. After a breakup, the boyfriend uploads the video to social media groups without her consent. Under Explanation 2, the boyfriend is guilty of voyeurism under s. 77.
distinctions: Watching/Capturing vs Dissemination: The offence is committed by watching or capturing alone; dissemination is an independent aggravating route.
Consensual capture vs Non-consensual dissemination (Explanation 2): Consent to take a picture does not imply consent to publish it.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an individual who installed a hidden recording device in a female hostel bathroom is liable under BNS s. 77.
Rule: Section 77 penalizes capturing the image of a woman engaging in a private act with expectation of privacy.
Application: A bathroom is a quintessential private space, and recording was clandestine.
Conclusion: The individual is guilty of voyeurism under s. 77.

shortAnswer: State BNS s. 77 definition of voyeurism.
Define private act and reasonable expectation of privacy.
State Explanation 2 on non-consensual dissemination (revenge porn).
tenMark: Introduction: Digital privacy and bodily sanctity.
Explanation 1 (private act) and Explanation 2 (consensual capture vs dissemination).

Comprehensive textual dissection of BNS s. 77.
The standard of 'reasonable expectation of privacy': public restrooms, hotel rooms, fitting rooms, and digital spaces.

keyTakeaways: Penalizes watching, capturing, or disseminating images of private acts.
Consensual capture does not permit dissemination (Explanation 2 covers revenge porn).
Punishment: 1 to 3 years (first conviction); 3 to 7 years (repeat conviction).
